title: A sample with three different animation interpolations -- five frames across its own declared span

criterion.says: A sample with three different animation interpolations

acceptanceClass.because: The framing rule's own direction over a subject that MOVES, so the comparison is taken at every frame of the declared grid rather than at one pose. Nothing here is analytic: what is compared is which pixels each side covers at each sampled time and what colour each body wears there.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

subjects.name: InterpolationTest
subjects.notes: Attributes NORMAL, POSITION, TEXCOORD_0. 9 animations over a declared span of 2 s. The file's own images are not read by this case: the material below declares its colours, so what is compared is where the geometry is at each frame and which body wears which row.

source.pinReason: the corpus-wide pin every manifest in this tree already cites

camera.derivation: The framing rule of src/gltf/Framing.h, quoted so the runner can refuse a mismatch rather than trust it. World bounds [-4.4, -2.1594625308162447, -1] to [4.4, 7.8, 1.0036747946388003], so centre = [0.0, 2.8202687345918775, 0.0018373973194001358] and radius = 6.720223333070925 m. yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from a 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. distance = radius / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 = 47.99344612554942, and the eye is centre + (cos20*cos35, sin20, cos20*sin35) * distance. clipStart is distance - radius and clipEnd is distance + radius. THE DEPTH WINDOW COVERS THE GRID AND THE CAMERA DOES NOT MOVE (`board:1433`, `board:1439`). This case's camera is deliberately elsewhere -- 13.794 m from the framing rule's answer, which is the 'or a metre or more' arm of the placement rule -- so raising its frame rate changes what the grid sweeps but must not change where it is seen from. The window is the swept radius about the grid's own centre, 8.537972820 m, taken about the DECLARED eye's distance to that centre, 47.346721586 m. [MEASURED] the old window cut a vertex at 40.997298 m against a near plane of 41.273223.
camera.note: THE ENGINE'S OWN ANSWER, QUOTED (board:1398). Every number here is read from the framing rule's output for this subject -- eye, aim, yfov and both clip planes -- rather than recomputed by the authoring helper, which bounded each primitive by the eight transformed corners of its local AABB and therefore always at least as loosely as the engine bounds the transformed vertices. A looser radius moves the eye back, and 93 cases declared a camera the rule does not derive. `ADerivedCameraIsTheFramingRuleAndNotAQuotation` recomputes all of it and refuses a mismatch, so what this declaration does is PIN the viewpoint, never choose it.

light.note: The material emits, so nothing has to arrive for the picture to exist.

world.note: Declared and zero rather than left factory, so the picture is a function of this manifest.

material.note: Emission, one colour per glTF material, keyed by the name the FILE gives it. A material a primitive does not name is keyed by `<default>`, which is the format's own word for the material an undefined `material` selects.

fps.note: FOUR FRAMES PER SECOND, AND THE RATE IS RAISED SO THE GRID FALLS BETWEEN KEYFRAMES. This file's keys sit at 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2 s; at 1 fps the grid ran 0, 1 and 2 s and [MEASURED] **every one of its three samples landed exactly on a key**. STEP, LINEAR and CUBICSPLINE all return the key's own value there, so the one case in this corpus named for interpolation -- and the ONLY case carrying a CUBICSPLINE sampler -- decided nothing about any of the three. At 4 fps the grid is 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1 s, so three of its five samples fall strictly between keys and the three curves are three different answers there. The rate is a declaration and no threshold moves.

frames.derivation: min(5, ceil(2 s * 4 fps) + 1) = 5, so the grid runs 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1 s.
frames.note: WHAT THIS GRID COVERS: the first half of the declared duration at four times the old density, chosen so the samples straddle keys rather than sit on them. Coverage of the SECOND half is given up for it, and that is the trade: a sample between keys decides an interpolation and a sample on a key decides a keyframe, and this case already had five keyframes and no interpolation.

default.note: The binary mask and the emitted colour in one render. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it. A still costs one frame, so the full 1280x720 is affordable here where an animated case has to buy its grid.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe with the sampler's seed moved. At one sample per pixel of a deterministic emission there is nothing for a seed to change, so any pixel that moves between these two renders is the oracle's own noise rather than a disagreement with us -- which is what makes this the instrument floor instead of an assumption about it.

notes: A coverage case over a moving subject. Its shading -- textures, metallic-roughness, any extension it declares -- is NOT what this decides; board:1363 records why no case takes the shading arm yet.

subjectFrameFraction.note: The fraction of the frame the subject's projected area covers at frame 0, recomputed by the runner on every run and refused on mismatch; seeded from that recomputation, so it pins the framing and detects drift.
